author: Andres Cardenal, CFA
title: Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) are two o
text:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) are two of the strongest and most profitable tech corporations in the world, and they are also direct competitors in different areas.
Alphabet stock has downright crushed Microsoft in the long term, with Alphabet delivering a cumulative return of nearly 2070% since its IPO in 2004 versus a cumulative return of 202% for Microsoft in the same period.
On the other hand, Microsoft is the clear winner over a shorter time frame: Since 2014 Microsoft has gained 144% versus a cumulative gain of 96% for Alphabet.
Which one is a better purchase going forward? 
Microsoft: The Empire Strikes Back Back in the nineties, Microsoft was the undisputed king in the tech industry, and the company was truly unparalleled in its financial and strategic resources. However, Microsoft didn’t have the right culture to succeed in an always changing and dynamic industry, and the company missed many of the most important tech trends over time, including game-changing innovations such as smartphones, social networks, and cloud computing.
Steve Ballmer, who was Microsoft CEO at the time, expressed his view, or his lack of view, about the iPhone in an interview with USA Today in 2007: “There's no chance that the iPhone is going to get any significant market share. No chance.” Ballmer said. 
These mistakes were tremendously expensive for Microsoft, and the company languished while competitors such as Alphabet and Apple ( AAPL ) flourished by embracing the main disruptive trends in technology.
But things changed for the better when Satya Nadella replaced Steve Ballmer as CEO in 2014. Nadella already was running Microsoft’s cloud division before being appointed as CEO, and focusing on the cloud was arguably his most important and effective contribution. 
Microsoft is currently the number two cloud vendor in the world behind Amazon ( AMZN ), and the company announced in its most recent earnings report that it reached its annual revenue run rate target of $20 billion for commercial cloud.
The company ended the quarter with 120 million monthly active users for Office 365. It has more than 530 million LinkedIn members, and Dynamics 365 customers grew 40% year over year. Azure compute usage more than doubled during the quarter, and revenue grew 90%.
These numbers show that the new and energized Microsoft is clearly moving in the right direction in terms of effective innovation and riding the key trends in the tech industry.
Alphabet: Barbarians At The Gate Or Never Ending Story? Alphabet is the global leader in online advertising thanks to its ubiquitous Google division, which generates the lion’s share of revenue and profits at the company level. Google owns seven different platforms with over 1 billion users each: Google Search, YouTube, Gmail, Google Play, Android, Chrome, and Maps.
The other bets division at Alphabet is a diversified group of businesses and projects in different areas. This includes investments in life sciences and robotics, high-speed internet, and research to explore aging and extending human lifespan, among several others.
It's hard to tell what kind of economic viability these projects will have in the short term. However, when seen as diversified portfolio of businesses in areas with massive potential for disruption, the long-term opportunities are clearly exciting.

Alphabet’s financial performance has been nothing short of outstanding over the years. The chart below shows the evolution of total revenue, free cash flow, and net income for the company in the last decade. The image is worth a thousand words. 
No company is completely immune to competition, and Alphabet is facing rising competitive pressure in key areas. Many consumers are increasingly relying on Amazon over Google when looking for products to purchase. In addition, Facebook ( FB ) is growing at a spectacular rate and stealing a share of the pie in online advertising.
Alphabet has the financial and strategic resources to protect the business from competition, but increasing competition is still a relevant risk factor to watch.
Looking Ahead Both companies have reported solid financial performance recently, but Alphabet is growing at a faster rate than Microsoft.
The online advertising leader reported a 24% increase in revenue during the third quarter of 2017, with earnings per share jumping by an impressive 32% year over year. As for Microsoft, total revenue grew 12%, and earnings per share increased 17% year over year last quarter.
The table below compares some key indicators for the two companies, including market capitalization, forward price to earnings, price to sales, price to free cash flow, expected growth rate in earnings over the coming five years, and price to earnings growth ratio.
Valuation levels based on current fundamentals are roughly similar. Alphabet is marginally more expensive than Microsoft in terms of forward price to earnings and price to sales, but it’s a bit cheaper when looking at price to free cash flow.

On the other hand, Alphabet is far superior in terms of growth expectations, since Wall Street analysts are expecting the company to grow earnings per share at 20.7% in the coming five years vs. an expected growth rate of 10.58% for Microsoft. This means Alphabet is much cheaper when incorporating growth into the valuation equation, as reflected by the price to earnings growth ratio.
Growth expectations from analysts are subject to errors and revisions, but it’s not too hard to envision Alphabet generating that kind of growth over the middle term. With revenue growing at 24% last quarter and profit margins expanding, the idea sounds quite reasonable.
Besides, Alphabet has $100.1 billion in cash and liquid investments on its balance sheet, and tax reform is allowing the company to repatriate that capital for a conveniently low cost. Alphabet could use that money to aggressively repurchase stock, and that would provide a big boost to earnings per share growth by reducing the amount of shares outstanding.
Microsoft has done a great job at recovering from its mistakes and jumpstarting financial performance over the past several years. Satya Nadella certainly deserves recognition for that.
In fact, it’s not by pure chance that Microsoft stock outperformed Alphabet since 2014. Market expectations for Microsoft were quite low when Nadella took the reins, and the company has clearly done better than expected.
However, Microsoft’s transformation already is incorporated into valuation to a good degree, and it’s hard to see how Microsoft stock could outperform Alphabet from current valuation levels.
Alphabet, on the other hand, looks fairly conveniently priced, if not downright undervalued considering the company’s quality and growth potential. Given to choose between Microsoft and Alphabet, the online advertising leader could offer superior gains in the years ahead.
